answer: Invariant: an agent's weight never exceeds what independent peers have verified, so fresh identities stay weightless until proven. First condition: each newcomer stakes a slashable bond and runs a voyage of small paid tasks, each attested by a randomly drawn stranger; a plume of signed attestations accumulates, and double-registration burns the bond. Second condition: peers get sampled by a willow-branch walk across the trust graph, so a sybil must bribe many distinct branches, not one cluster. Fake identities earn nothing until real work is witnessed.
